title: Test and Scan Tooling Readiness Gate
goal: Add a safe, deterministic tooling readiness gate for stronger local testing and scanning coverage without running live target scans.
scope: React v2 visual/accessibility testing, API contract fuzzing against local FastAPI fixtures, SAST/dependency/secret scan readiness, and ZAP automation isolation.
generation_reason: The 2026-05-11 readiness pass found that extra online-supported tools would improve coverage, but integration is larger than a crash fix and must be safety-bounded.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Build a readiness/reporting gate first; do not turn the task into live scanning, tool installation, or broad dependency modernization beyond documented review-only findings.
constraints.safety_reframe: Readiness and local-fixture validation only. Do not scan live public targets, expand scope, run active DAST without explicit operator authorization, materialize credentials, approve proposals, mutate runtime gates, or bypass kill-switch behavior.

success_criteria: A deterministic tool-readiness command reports installed/missing tool status for ZAP, Semgrep, Schemathesis, Trivy, Gitleaks, pip-audit, npm audit, Lighthouse CI, and Playwright accessibility/visual support.
ZAP readiness handles the existing localhost daemon safely by using a dedicated automation home or daemon API and does not race the default ZAP home directory.
Semgrep readiness runs with sanitized empty proxy environment variables and records a clear operator-facing blocker if rules or network access are unavailable.
React v2 coverage includes at least one accessibility or visual-regression guard for clipped controls / crash-recovery screens.
API contract fuzzing is documented or wired only against local FastAPI fixtures using the generated OpenAPI schema.
Dependency and secret scan commands produce review-only artifacts and do not auto-fix breaking upgrades.
The Vite/esbuild npm audit advisory is tracked with an explicit compatibility plan instead of `npm audit fix --force` being applied blindly.
Release-readiness docs explain which scans are active gates, diagnostic gates, or future optional gates.

acceptance_criteria: Tool readiness checks are deterministic and local-safe.
No live target DAST/SAST against customer systems is performed.

out_of_scope: Running active scans against public targets.
Installing uncontrolled tooling during active assessments.
Auto-fixing dependency upgrades that require breaking framework changes.
Bypassing approval, scope/ROE, runtime binding, credential protection, or kill-switch behavior.
